overview:
Honest answer: nobody can know in advance how many tokens an arbitrary software task will consume, and none of the three repos tries to. GSD's '~50% context per plan' is a prompt heuristic with a lookup table of guessed percentages keyed to file counts and task type (agents/gsd-planner.md, Task Sizing and scope_estimation). The only mechanical check on it is the plan-checker's count of tasks and files per plan (2-3 tasks, 5-8 files target; 4 tasks or 10 files warn; 5+ tasks or 15+ files block), which is itself an LLM reading a table. GSD does contain real measurement code, but it is aimed elsewhere: sdk/src/query/prompt-budget.ts trims review prompts to a token budget using ceil(chars/4), and hooks/gsd-statusline.js + hooks/gsd-context-monitor.js read Claude Code's context_window.remaining_percentage at run time and inject warnings at 35% and 25% remaining. Nothing records measured peak per plan and feeds it back into sizing. The 50% figure is not derived from any measurement in the repo.

Ralph's rule ('each story must be completable in ONE iteration / one context window', ralph/skills/ralph/SKILL.md; README 'Small Tasks') is advisory prose with examples of right-sized and too-big stories plus a checklist item; ralph.sh has no estimator and no overflow handling (the README only mentions an Amp autoHandoff setting at 90% context for oversized stories, which is a host feature). Its real mechanism is the fresh-context-per-iteration loop with prd.json passes flags and progress.txt, so a failed oversized story simply fails its checks and retries. BMAD's 900-1600 token 'scope standard' (skills/bmad-build/workflow.md SCOPE STANDARD; bmad-build-auto/plan-template.md and step-02-plan.md) measures the size of the PLAN DOCUMENT the implementer reads, not the cost of doing the work, and explicitly states 'Neither limit is a gate. Both are proposals with user override.' The one mechanical piece is step-02: if the plan file exceeds 1600 tokens, add an 'oversized' warning to frontmatter and continue anyway. How the token count is computed is left to the model.

So the practical truth is: pre-step estimates are weak priors built from the predictable components (fixed overhead, files you can enumerate and measure, capped tool outputs); the unpredictable components (exploration, retries, reasoning, test noise) are bounded by caps and detected after the fact via telemetry. A sound harness therefore estimates cheaply, measures every step, calibrates its estimates against its own history, and has a cheap deterministic response (split, clip, checkpoint, resume) when an estimate is wrong, rather than trusting the estimate. Anthropic's own guidance (Effective context engineering for AI agents) gives no formula for estimating task tokens; it is qualitative (attention budget, context rot, compaction, sub-agents returning 1-2k token summaries). The Claude Code docs likewise point to measurement (/context, /usage, statusline fields, OpenTelemetry) not prediction.

Era caveat: the 50/70 'degradation curve' in GSD and the 900-1600 token plan size are prompt-era heuristics with no cited measurements; Chroma's Context Rot study (July 2025, 18 models incl. Claude 4, GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5) supports the direction (reliability falls as input grows, non-uniformly) but not these specific thresholds, and says nothing about Claude 5-generation models. For Sonnet 5.5/Opus 5.5 with 200k-1M windows, treat every percentage as a tunable parameter calibrated from your own telemetry, not a constant.
howItWorks: GSD planning: gsd-planner.md tells the planner to 'Estimate effort in context window cost, not time', targets ~50% of context per plan, 2-3 tasks per plan, and 10-30% per task; the cost 'signals' are file-count buckets (0-3 files = ~10-15%, 4-6 = ~20-30%, 7+ = ~40%+). [repo-proven as prompt text; no measurement behind the numbers]

GSD plan-checker (Dimension 5 Scope Sanity) counts tasks and modified files per plan and compares to thresholds (target/warning/blocker). It is the only quasi-mechanical gate and it is executed by an LLM agent, not a script. [repo-proven]

GSD overflow response at planning time: planner may return '## PHASE SPLIT RECOMMENDED' and the workflow (plan-phase.md step 9b) offers split vs 'Proceed anyway (planner will attempt all, quality may degrade past 50% context)'. [repo-proven, advisory, user-prompted]

GSD at execution time: gsd-statusline.js receives Claude Code's statusline JSON (context_window.remaining_percentage, total_tokens), writes /tmp/claude-ctx-<session>.json; gsd-context-monitor.js (PostToolUse hook) reads it, ignores data older than 60 s, and when remaining <= 35% injects a WARNING and at <= 25% a CRITICAL as additionalContext (debounced to every 5 tool calls, escalation bypasses debounce); at CRITICAL in a GSD project it spawns 'gsd-tools state record-session' to leave a resume breadcrumb. The message is advisory ('Avoid starting new complex work'), it does not stop the agent. [repo-proven]

GSD orchestrator hygiene: references/context-budget.md says never inline large files into subagent prompts, read frontmatter only when context_window < 500k, delegate heavy work. Tiers PEAK 0-30 / GOOD 30-50 / DEGRADING 50-70 / POOR 70+. [repo-proven prompt text]

Ralph: ralph/skills/ralph/SKILL.md says each story must fit one iteration; ralph.sh spawns a fresh Claude/Amp per iteration; completion is judged by checks and the passes flag in prd.json; progress.txt and AGENTS.md carry learnings. No estimator, no overflow detector. [repo-proven; advisory]

BMAD (bmad-build / bmad-build-auto): plan must target a single user-facing goal in 900-1600 tokens; step-02 adds 'oversized' to plan frontmatter warnings when the plan file exceeds 1600 tokens, and 'multiple-goals' when step-01 flagged it, then continues. Both limits are 'proposals with user override'. [repo-proven; advisory warning only]

Proposed for your harness, pre-step: a script computes est_tokens = fixed_overhead + sum(token_count(files the step must read)) * read_multiplier + expected_output_allowance, using the Anthropic count_tokens endpoint (free, exact tokenizer for the target model) or a local chars-per-token ratio calibrated per model. [proposal]

Proposed, during step: the host's own telemetry is the ground truth. Claude Code exposes context_window fields to statusline scripts and writes per-request usage (input, output, cache_creation, cache_read) in session transcript JSONL; the script reads them at step end to compute measured_peak_context = max over requests of (input + cache_read + cache_creation). [proposal built on documented host facts; verify field names against your CLI version]

Proposed, post-step: append est vs measured to a ledger, fit a per-(step_kind, model) ratio, and use the p80 of measured/estimated as the safety multiplier for the next estimate. Split rule and overflow handling are described in the examples. [proposal]

examples.label: GSD planner: the sizing text (verbatim)
examples.source: get-shit-done/agents/gsd-planner.md (Task Sizing section; Quality Degradation Curve and scope_estimation near line 149 and 384)
examples.text:
## Task Sizing

Each task targets **10–30% context consumption**.

| Context Cost | Action |
|--------------|--------|
| < 10% context | Too small — combine with a related task |
| 10-30% context | Right size — proceed |
| > 30% context | Too large — split into two tasks |

**Context cost signals (use these, not time estimates):**
- Files modified: 0-3 = ~10-15%, 4-6 = ~20-30%, 7+ = ~40%+ (split)
- New subsystem: ~25-35%
- Migration + data transform: ~30-40%
- Pure config/wiring: ~5-10%

**Rule:** Plans should complete within ~50% context. More plans, smaller scope, consistent quality. Each plan: 2-3 tasks max.

(Only three legitimate reasons to split: 'Context cost: implementation would consume >50% of a single agent's context window', missing information, dependency conflict.)

examples.label: GSD plan-checker: the only mechanical-looking gate
examples.text:
**Question:** Will plans complete within context budget?

**Process:**
1. Count tasks per plan
2. Estimate files modified per plan
3. Check against thresholds

| Metric | Target | Warning | Blocker |
|--------|--------|---------|---------|
| Tasks/plan | 2-3 | 4 | 5+ |
| Files/plan | 5-8 | 10 | 15+ |
| Total context | ~50% | ~70% | 80%+ |

examples.label: GSD runtime measurement: the 35%/25% context monitor
GSD's only token estimator: chars/4 for trimming review prompts, not for sizing tasks
Ralph: the whole sizing rule
examples.text:
Each PRD item should be small enough to complete in one context window. If a task is too big, the LLM runs out of context before finishing and produces poor code.

Right-sized stories:
- Add a database column and migration
- Add a UI component to an existing page

Too big (split these):
- "Build the entire dashboard"
- "Add authentication"
- "Refactor the API"

(SKILL.md: '**Each story must be completable in ONE Ralph iteration (one context window).**' plus checklist item 'Each story is completable in one iteration (small enough)'. No script enforces it.)

examples.label: BMAD: scope standard and the only mechanical hook
examples.text:
A plan should target a **single user-facing goal** within **900–1600 tokens**:
- **900–1600 tokens**: Optimal range for LLM consumption. Below 900 risks ambiguity; above 1600 risks context-rot in implementation agents.
- **Neither limit is a gate.** Both are proposals with user override.

step-02-plan.md: 6. Warning check. If step-01 carried `multiple-goals`, add it to `{plan_file}` frontmatter `warnings`. If `{plan_file}` exceeds 1600 tokens, add `oversized` to frontmatter `warnings`. Continue either way.

examples.label: Cost components of one step and how predictable each is
examples.source: proposal (component list from Claude Code docs: costs, context; prompt caching; thinking)
examples.text:
FIXED, near-exact, known before start:
  system prompt + CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md + skills listing + tool schemas (MCP schemas can be 5-20k each per GSD context-budget.md; deferred by default in current Claude Code)
  step packet/prompt itself (you wrote it: count it)
ENUMERABLE, estimable within ~1.2-2x:
  files the step must read (you know the paths; tokenize them)
  files edited (read + the edit payload; whole-file rewrites cost the whole file)
CAPPABLE, bounded by you:
  test/build/lint output (pipe through head/grep; docs show a PreToolUse filter hook)
  tool output generally (clip in a hook)
UNPREDICTABLE, observe only:
  exploration (grep/glob/read fan-out when the packet is vague)
  thinking tokens (adaptive on Sonnet/Opus 5.x; cannot be turned off; billed as output)
  retries after failures; debugging detours
  compaction events (re-read cost, cache rebuild)
NOTE: cost vs peak context differ. Context peak = what fills the window; billed tokens = every request resends history (cache reads), so a long step costs more than its peak suggests.

examples.label: Proposed step record with estimate and measurement fields
Proposed estimator output (script, before the step)
examples.text:
$ harness estimate S-014 --model claude-sonnet-5-5
fixed overhead (system+tools+AGENTS.md+packet)   24,000  (measured last 20 steps, p50)
read set: 2 files, 9,900 tok x 2.0 reread/partial  19,800
edit set: 1 file x full rewrite allowance          6,100
tool-output cap: 4 bash calls x 5,000 hard clip   20,000
reasoning+reply allowance (kind=implement p50)    18,000
subtotal                                          87,900
calibration p80 ratio (kind=implement, n=23)      x1.15 -> 101,100
budget 150,000 (15% of 1M; 50% of hard stop)      FITS (67%)
confidence: medium (n=23, ratio spread 0.8-1.9)
unknowns: no failing-test list yet; grep fan-out not modeled

examples.label: Proposed split rule and overflow policy
examples.text:
PRE-STEP: if est_tokens > budget_tokens OR read_set > N files OR packet tokens > cap -> script refuses to start; emits 'split' packet with the read set partitioned by directory/module (script-owned, not LLM-owned). Cap depth: split_count <= 2 then escalate to owner.
DURING: host hook reads context remaining; at 65% used (WARN) inject 'finish current edit, commit, write handoff'; at 75% (HARD) script kills/stops the step after the next tool call, records overflow_action=checkpoint.
POST-OVERFLOW: next step is a resume packet: git diff stat + handoff file + remaining acceptance criteria only (no history). Count it as a split child (parent_step set, split_count+1).
POST-STEP: ratio = measured.peak_context / est_tokens; append to ledger; refit calibration_ratio = p80 of last 30 ratios per (kind, model).

examples.label: Proposed calibration loop (script, sketch)
examples.text:
# after each step
ledger.append(step_id, kind, model, est_tokens, peak_context, outcome)
rows = ledger.last(kind, model, n=30)
if len(rows) >= 8:
    ratios = sorted(r.peak / r.est for r in rows if r.outcome in ('pass','overflow'))
    calibration_ratio = percentile(ratios, 80)   # p80, not mean: overflow costs more than waste
else:
    calibration_ratio = 1.5                      # conservative prior until data exists
# drift alarm: if median ratio moves >25% across a model/CLI upgrade, reset to prior and re-learn
# (tokenizer changed ~30% between pre-4.7 and 4.7+ models per Anthropic docs)

pitfalls: Treating GSD's 50% as measured. It is an unreferenced heuristic; the file-count-to-percent buckets (0-3 files = 10-15% etc.) are guesses with no calibration data in the repo, and the 30/50/70 degradation tiers are asserted, not cited. Do not copy the numbers; copy the idea of a budget and make the numbers yours.

GSD's context monitor is advisory. The code comment says 'stop immediately' but the injected text says avoid new complex work and inform the user; a script harness that needs a hard stop must enforce it itself.

chars/4 (GSD, Aider-style folklore) is English-prose-oriented. Code, JSON and minified text tokenize differently, and Anthropic documents that Claude 4.7+ models, including Fable/Mythos 5.x, use a tokenizer that yields about 30% more tokens for the same text than older models. Any ratio from old blog posts or old ledgers is stale; recount per model with the free count_tokens endpoint (which is itself labelled an estimate, small variance, no server tools/MCP connector, no URL-sourced images or documents).

Estimating read cost as file size undercounts: agents grep, re-read, read partial ranges and read neighbors. Use a multiplier learned from history, and measure tool-result tokens separately from model output.

Peak context is not billed cost. Every request resends history (mostly cache reads); a step that peaks at 120k with 41 requests bills far more input than 120k. Size by peak for quality/overflow decisions; track billed tokens separately for budget decisions. Cache misses after idle gaps (5 min to 1 h TTL) re-bill the full context.

Hidden fixed overhead: tool schemas, MCP instructions, AGENTS.md/skills listings, hook-injected context. GSD's own docs say a few MCP servers can cost 20k+ tokens per turn each (older behavior; current Claude Code defers MCP tool definitions by default). Measure the empty-session baseline with /context or a no-op step instead of assuming.

Thinking tokens on Sonnet 5.5/Opus 5.5 are always on and adaptive; effort level changes cost a lot and is not predictable from the task text. Record effort per step in the ledger or ratios will not transfer.

Chroma's context-rot results were on 18 models up to roughly Claude 4 / GPT-4.1 / Gemini 2.5 with simple synthetic and QA tasks; degradation is non-uniform (distractors, needle similarity, position). It justifies keeping context lean but does not give a threshold, and nothing here is measured on Claude 5-generation models. Anthropic's post says the same qualitatively ('attention budget') and gives no estimation method.

Percentages of window are meaningless across window sizes. 50% of 200k (100k) and 50% of 1M (500k) behave differently; GSD itself branches behavior on context_window >= 500k. Budget in absolute tokens per model and keep window as a separate field. Claude Code also reserves an autocompact buffer (GSD hard-codes 16.5% in its statusline; verify against your version) so 'remaining' is not the same as usable.

Splitting has its own cost: each child pays fixed overhead again (the GSD token tax per fresh context, ~24k in the illustrative record) and loses cross-file understanding; over-splitting wastes more than occasional overflow. BMAD's single-goal rule (never split cross-layer details of one user goal) guards against this.

Ralph's retry-on-failure model hides overflow: an oversized story that runs out of context just looks like a failed check, so you cannot distinguish 'too big' from 'wrong'. Record overflow/compaction events explicitly.
Do not let the model judge its own context use ('I think I used about half'). Use host telemetry; models are poor at estimating their own token counts.
modelEra: Era flags. 4k-32k-window era: any rule that computes 'fits the window' by counting a whole repo or truncating files (old Aider default map of 1k tokens is a deliberate small-context design; its --map-tokens budget and PageRank map are still sensible as a technique, but the numbers are 2023-24 vintage). Ralph's 'one context window' rule was written for Amp/Claude Code at ~200k and for older models; it is still directionally right but not a size. GSD references/context-budget.md branches on 200k vs 500k+ windows and strips content for sub-200k windows, so its constants are explicitly pre-1M. Claude 4/GPT-4.1/Gemini 2.5 era: the Chroma study models, and the 30/50/70% quality tiers (plausibly from Claude 3.5-4 behavior; unverified). Claude 5-generation specifics (documented by Anthropic, verified by fetch on 2026-10-11): token counting API supports claude-opus-5-5; Claude 4.7+ and Fable/Mythos 5.x use a newer tokenizer giving about 30% more tokens for the same text, so recount per model; Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable always use thinking (cannot be disabled), with adaptive budgets steered by effort; Claude Code prompt cache TTL is 1 h on subscription and 5 min on API/credits; MCP tool definitions are deferred by default; statusline scripts receive context_window and prompt_cache objects; /context and /usage report live numbers. What is era-independent: the cost components list, measure-after-every-step, calibrate to your own history, deterministic split/resume, and clipping tool output.
whatWouldChange: 1. Add a step ledger (JSONL) written by the script, not the model: step_id, kind, model, effort, est_tokens, est_basis, measured.peak_context, measured billed tokens by type, requests, compactions, outcome, split_count, parent_step. Source measurements from transcript usage blocks or the statusline/OTel feed at step end. 2. Add a script-run 'estimate' command invoked before dispatch that tokenizes the declared read set (count_tokens for the target model, or a per-model chars/token ratio measured from the same API), adds measured fixed overhead and tool-output caps, applies the calibrated p80 ratio, and writes est_basis. 3. Make the step packet declare its read set and expected edit set (paths), so estimation is mechanical; refuse to dispatch steps with no declared read set above a size, and flag vague packets as high-variance. 4. Enforce tool-output caps with a PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook (head/grep filters for tests, builds, logs) so the CAPPABLE component is really capped; log truncation. 5. Own the thresholds in the script: pre-step refuse-and-split when est > budget; during-step hook reads context remaining and at the soft threshold injects a wrap-up instruction, at the hard threshold the script ends the step after the current tool call and writes a checkpoint; GSD's 35%/25% remaining is a reasonable starting point to tune, but make it absolute tokens per model. 6. Split rule owned by script: partition the read set by module/directory, cap split depth (e.g. 2) then escalate; resume packets carry diff stat + handoff + remaining acceptance criteria only. 7. Calibration loop: per (kind, model, effort) keep the last 30 est/measured ratios; use p80 as multiplier once n >= 8, conservative prior before; alert and reset on model/CLI version change. 8. Replace percent-of-window language in packets with absolute token budgets and record context_window separately. 9. Keep a small set of golden calibration steps (fixed tasks) re-run on each model release to detect tokenizer/thinking drift. 10. Evaluate by outcome: overflow rate, split rate, wasted-overhead share, and estimate error (median and p90 of measured/est), all from the ledger.
